subject: Dedicated Reserve & Burst: hardware tradeoffs and fallback playbook
messages:
From: Evan Park <evan.park@nebulacorp.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-06-12T14:05:00Z
Subject: Sizing question: long-context + spikes (Nebula)

Hi Soojin,

We ran a quick evaluation of the model family you recommended and have two main workload characteristics:
- A subset of requests are very memory-heavy (long multi-document context, up to ~70k tokens, support for retrieval + memory).
- Most traffic is short (500-2,000 tokens) with high QPS during business hours, and large diurnal spikes around product launches.

Target SLOs: 95th latency < 400ms for short flows, and best-effort for long-context flows (we can tolerate higher tail latency for those).
We need a recommendation for Dedicated: H100 vs A100 vs L4 mix, how much reserved capacity to commit vs burst, and fallback policies. Also include ops constraints: pre-warm needs, cache hit assumptions, and cost ballpark.

Can you sketch a plan and a recommended initial reserve commitment? We have an internal pilot window in July to validate.

Thanks,
Evan
Evan Park
CTO, Nebula Corp
From: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
To: Evan Park <evan.park@nebulacorp.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-06-12T15:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Sizing question: long-context + spikes (Nebula)

Hi Evan — thanks for the clear workload summary. High level thoughts below; I want to confirm a few numbers (QPS percentiles, avg tokens per call, and expected prefix reuse) but this is a conservative starting plan that balances memory needs and cost.

TL;DR: Reserve for the steady-state that supports predictable peak QPS for short flows on A100 + an H100 reserve slab sized for concurrent long-context jobs; provision L4s in the burst pool for low-cost, low-latency routing of stateless short calls.

Key tradeoffs and rationale:
- H100: best for very long-context, memory-heavy workloads where large VRAM and tensor-core perf reduce OOMs and avoid sharding. Use H100s for pinned long sessions and retrieval-heavy pipelines.
- A100: best middle ground for most 8k-32k contexts with strong throughput; cheaper than H100 for batchy workloads and good for quantized medium-context models.
- L4: much lower cost and great for short, latency-sensitive calls when using quantized smaller variants. Not suitable when >32k context or when KV cache spans large working sets.

Initial reserve suggestion (subject to your confirmation of QPS):
- Reserve commit: 40% of steady compute on A100 (throughput), 40% on H100 (long-context headroom), 20% on L4 (low-cost baseline).
- Example starting counts (pilot scale): Reserve 8x H100, 16x A100, 8x L4. Burst pool: add 12 L4 + 8 A100 capacity on-demand.

Operational notes:
- KV/prefix cache: use dedicated warm H100 slots for pinned sessions; rely on our prefix-caching layer to avoid recomputing retrieval context where possible. Cache hit rate assumptions: 30-50% for your retrieval flows (please confirm).
- Quantization: enable Q4/INT4 for L4 and A100 where model fidelity permits; keep H100 at FP16/AMP for memory-intensive flows.
- Autoscale windows: pre-warm burst pool 2–3 minutes ahead for product-launch traffic if you can provide a traffic prediction feed.

Cost/ballpark: monthly reserved commit cost depends on region and term; rough heuristic: H100 slot ~3–4x A100 cost; L4 ~0.15–0.25x A100. I will follow up with a detailed cost estimate once we have percentiles.

Next steps: if you can share a 48-hour traffic sample (QPS by minute + token histogram) we’ll run a simulated runbook and provide a concrete reserve vs burst sizing and estimated cost. I attached a short appendix for the plan.

Cheers,
Soojin Lee
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
From: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-06-13T10:12:00Z
Subject: FW: Nebula sizing — propose numbers for pilot (internal)

Team — forwarding Evan’s note. He asked for a concrete pilot-sized reserve + burst layout and an ops playbook. My initial thought is below; please critique and give final numbers we can present to the customer.

Proposal (pilot scale, region: us-west):
1) Workload breakdown assumptions (please confirm with Evan):
   - Short flows: 82% of calls, avg 900 tokens, P95 QPS during business hours: 320 req/s
   - Medium flows: 15% of calls, avg 6k tokens, can batch up to 2x
   - Long flows: 3% of calls, avg 45k tokens (retrieval + memory), long-lived sessions
2) Sizing math (conservative):
   - Short flows <=2k tokens: target 95th latency 300–400ms; per-A100 slot (8x concurrency with batching) ~45 req/s depending on model; use L4 for lower-cost stateless routing where model variant is smaller.
   - Long flows: H100 slot handles ~1–2 concurrent long sessions (memory constrained) — size headroom accordingly.
3) Recommended initial reserve counts (pilot):
   - Reserve: 10 A100 slots (steady short/medium), 6 H100 slots (pinned long-context), 6 L4 slots (baseline cheap routing)
   - Burst pool: 12 L4, 6 A100, 4 H100 (fast fallback with pre-warm triggers)
4) Fallback and routing policy:
   - Primary policy: route short calls to L4 when model size permits; failover to A100 if latency or fidelity thresholds not met.
   - Long calls: route to H100; if H100 capacity constrained, route to A100 with degraded memory window and notify caller (graceful degradation).
   - Soft quota: enforce token caps on long sessions to avoid runaway KV cache growth; surface telemetry for spikes.
5) Quantization and model variants:
   - L4: Q4/INT4 quantized 13B–70B variants for short paths.
   - A100: Q4/Amp mixed for most medium contexts.
   - H100: FP16 preferred for >32k contexts; avoid extreme quantization to reduce hallucination risk.
6) Reliability ops:
   - Pre-warm triggers from Nebula’s product-launch webhook (2–3 min lead) to scale burst pools.
   - Keep at least 1 H100 slot as hot spare in region for emergency long-context failover.

Ask: Dev — can you run a micro-sim with those numbers + a 48h traffic CSV (format per link below) and return expected tail latency and estimated token cost for 1M tokens? Aditya — sanity check the slot concurrency and memory assumptions (especially H100 long-session concurrency).

Thanks — Soojin
From: dev_patel@redwood.ai
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-06-13T13:48:00Z
Subject: Re: FW: Nebula sizing — propose numbers for pilot (internal)

+Notes from ops POV:
- Pre-warm: 120s is realistic for A100; 90–120s for H100 warm-up depending on model weight and checkpointing. We need to avoid very short-lived warm cycles because the cost of warming H100s is non-trivial.
- Pod density: aim for 1 H100 per pod for pinned sessions and 2–4 A100 per pod depending on instance class and networking. L4s can be multi-tenant.
- Autoscale policy: prefer controlled step-ups (25% increments) during launches; full burst only for <10m durations.
- OOM/guardrails: enforce per-session memory guard and automatic fallback strip (trim context + re-run retrieval) when >85% memory.

Quick sims (rough): with Soojin’s pilot counts and workload assumptions, expected P95 latency for short flows: ~380ms if 60% of short flows hit L4, ~310ms if 80% hit L4. Long-context concurrency will need an H100:1–2 session ratio; 6 H100 slots covers up to ~10–12 concurrent long sessions (with some batching).

Cost delta note: if Nebula opts to shift 10% of short traffic off A100 to L4, monthly token-related cost decreases ~18–22% on our model.

I’ll run the sim across 48h sample once they upload. I’ll also produce a quick ops runbook for launch-day scaling.

— Dev
From: soojin_lee@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Sizing question: long-context + spikes (Nebula)

Hi Evan — looping back with a concrete pilot proposal and the ops playbook attached. Key points for the pilot (summary):

1) Pilot reserve & burst (us-west):
   - Reserve commit: 10 A100, 6 H100, 6 L4
   - Burst pool (on-demand): 6 A100, 4 H100, 12 L4
2) Routing & fallback:
   - Short calls -> L4 (quantized) -> fallback to A100 if fidelity or latency breach
   - Medium calls -> A100 primary
   - Long calls -> H100 primary; fallback to A100 with degraded context trimming and notification
3) Ops & pre-warm:
   - 120s pre-warm for A100; 90–120s H100 warm window.
   - Keep 1 hot-spare H100 in region.
4) Expected outcomes & costs:
   - P95 short-flow latency target: ~300–380ms depending on L4 hit rate.
   - Cost leverage: L4 usage for short calls reduces token unit cost by ~20% vs A100-only routing.

Next steps:
- If you’re comfortable, approve the pilot reserve counts and we’ll provision and run a 2-week pilot where we ingest your 48h sample and validate tail-latency and cost.
- I attached an appendix (Reserve-Burst-HW-Appendix.pdf) with the detailed slot math, example traffic CSV format, and pre-warm webhook spec.

Approve below or let me know what to change and we’ll iterate quickly.

Best,
Soojin Lee
